changes.summary: limit setup to the attention preset
breaking: `bee setup` no longer installs BV recipes. Its success receipt removes `recipes`, and failure receipts remove `recipesInstalled`; Beeswax now owns Hive's viewer recipes.

adoption.text:
update consumers that read the removed recipe fields or rely on Bee setup to install
views. Upgrade the suite and use `beeswax update --yes` for the required `_hive_` recipes, following
`beeswax changelog` for project-contract and prompt adoption. Personal recipes remain untouched.

changes.summary: honor workflow retirement during request publication
changes.body:
Driver attachment, stage dispatch and retries now check native workflow anchors
and publication readiness. A retired run, unfinished settlement or contradictory
unmanaged provenance cannot admit a new request. Existing request acknowledgment,
resolution and replacement history remain separate from workflow outcomes.
breaking:
request publication refuses terminal or inconsistent workflow
scope rather than treating any closed anchor as completed work. Unmarked
historical closures do not acquire an inferred successful outcome.

adoption.text:
upgrade Bee with Busy Bee and Colony. Resolve reported authority or
publication failures from retained evidence; a retry does not authorize reopening
or retiring workflow work, and no bulk historical migration is required.

changes.summary: introduce workflow-filtering views, superseded by Beeswax ownership
changes.body:
This change introduced separate ordinary-work and workflow views for the
`busybee-workflow` classification. Later in the 0.9.0 source history, commit 98ce7cb8 moved Hive's
views from Bee setup to Beeswax under `_hive_` names. The earlier generic-view
installer and its `bee setup` adoption step are superseded.

For the released behavior, follow the setup entry above and `beeswax changelog`.
Beeswax preserves generic/personal recipes. Viewer setup changes no issue labels;
historical workflow classification requires a separately authorized backfill.

changes.summary: remove auxiliary assessment and inactivity reports
changes.body:
Remove `bee system assess` and `bee system report`. `bee system` now exposes
Busy Bee stage dispatch. Managed bees continue to deliver answers through
`bee response` and report execution completion through `bee finish`.
breaking: `bee system assess` and `bee system report` are removed. Hive's `nurse`, `post-run-drone` and `drone` kinds are no longer available.

adoption.text:
remove callers of the retired report commands. This repository's
`nurse`, `post-run-drone` and `drone` kinds are removed; update submissions or
kind selectors that name them. Install Bee with matching Colony,
colony-runtime, colony-worker and colony-watchdog executables, following
Colony's configuration and coordinated-restart guidance.

changes.body:
Hive's nurse again answers explicitly assigned colony-health questions without
automatic batch, topic-curation or investigation authority. Its configured
gpt-6.1-sol model and high reasoning effort remain unchanged. Changes, retries
and evidence curation require ct's authorization.

Required: remove `auto_nurse` from canonical `.hive/bees.toml` before running
the new Bee binary; shared configuration validation rejects that removed key.
Deploy the restored nurse role with the matching runtime. New requests capture
the updated role; existing captured recipes remain unchanged. Discover the
role with `bee kinds nurse --verbose` and submit explicit assignments through
`bee spawn --help`.

changes.summary: generalize Hive's drone role for focused workflow assignments
changes.body:
Hive's configured drone kind takes permitted actions and delivery from its
assigned workflow or private protocol. Ordinary workflow runs use Bee responses
and completion reporting; private inactivity reviews retain their active/inactive
verdict protocol. Existing captured recipes retain their original role.

Optional: adopting repositories can use a similarly generic role when assigning
their drone kind to ordinary review workflows. The role itself grants no recovery
authority; keep the action scope in each supplied workflow or private protocol.

changes.summary: distinguish role selection from workflow sequence
changes.body:
Delegation guidance selects a role by its remit and a workflow by the
task, routing submission options to bee spawn --help. Hive's Architect,
Bookworm and Reviewer prompts retain their professional judgement and
authority while removing repeated workflow and delivery procedure.
Architect advice remains available for focused integration or unblock
questions; Hive's simplified feature workflow no longer requires a second
Architect gate or receipt ledger for every delivery.

Optional: review custom role prompts for duplicated task sequence or
delivery instructions. Existing kind defaults, overrides and permissions
are unchanged.

changes.summary: give the nurse scoped batch-audit instructions
changes.body:
Hive's nurse now uses gpt-6.1-sol with high reasoning. Automatic audit briefs
authorize provisional health records and bounded read-only investigations,
require exact report coverage and verified delivery, and preserve examined
code, claims and request outcomes. Manual health advice remains advice unless
its assignment explicitly grants curation or investigation scope.

Required for automatic audits: deploy the updated nurse role and Colony
runtime together. New requests capture the current role; existing captured
recipes remain unchanged. Use `bee kinds nurse --verbose` to inspect defaults
and the Colony guide for activation. No action is required for manual advice.

changes.summary: guide workflow drivers through focused brief reads
changes.body:
Managed workflow drivers read the full native run brief on entry and each
active task brief once per visit. They refresh briefs when relevant scope,
state or authority changes and use compact Busy Bee views between reads.
This keeps caller completion instructions and stage authority explicit.

Optional: align custom driver prompts with this reading procedure and use
`busybee show --help` to discover frozen instruction expansion.

`bee retry REQUEST --resume-cancelled` permits deliberate replacement of a
cancelled request with unfinished work and no existing replacement. It retains
the workflow assignment, captures current kind defaults and explicit overrides,
and creates a fresh identity bound to the submitting host. Human/HITL
reservations, conflicting open requests and existing task claims retain their
normal treatment. Acknowledged failures remain ineligible.

The old request retains its cancellation, closure time and identity. `bee status`
exposes replacement IDs while the old disposition stays cancelled/resolved and
outside failure attention. Interrupted publication retains confirmed IDs;
repeating a superseded request repairs query labels and refuses a duplicate.

Optional: after verifying the old execution has stopped and deciding to resume
its assignment, read `bee retry --help` and invoke the explicit option with any
needed recipe overrides. Request closure alone is not process verification.

Required when adopting this recovery path: install Bee and Busy Bee from the
same updated Hive revision. Keep Bee's Colony CLI, runtime, worker and watchdog
companions together. Coordinate active work before deliberately restarting an
upgraded daemon; follow `colony daemon restart --help` with its retained selection.

changes.summary: group workflow and observer protocols under system
changes.body:
Busy Bee stage dispatch uses `bee system dispatch-stage`. Colony's auxiliary
observers submit through `bee system assess` and `bee system report`. The former
top-level paths are removed. Ordinary workers continue to use `bee finish`.

Required: upgrade Bee, Busy Bee and Colony together. Update custom integration
calls and observer prompts to the system paths; use `bee system --help` for the
protocols and their callers.
breaking: group workflow and observer protocols under system

adoption.text:
upgrade Bee, Busy Bee and Colony together. Update custom integration
calls and observer prompts to the system paths; use `bee system --help` for the
protocols and their callers.

changes.summary: add an operational Architect to Hive's bee catalogue
changes.body:
Hive's repository configuration adds a read-only Pi/Astra-high Architect
for feature continuity review and task unblocking. Detailed code/test review
remains Reviewer's role; Librarian retains architectural memory.

Optional: adopt the repository kind and specialist protocol with a compatible
Pi formula. Installing Bee alone does not copy repository kind configuration.

The `bee list` command has been removed.

Required: update `bee list` callers to use focused native Beads queries for
request discovery, then use exact request IDs with `bee status`, `bee result`
or `bee stop`. Read each command's focused `--help` before use.

changes.summary: clarify workflow result notes for stage completion
changes.body: `bee response --help` identifies workflow notes as Busy Bee's original `{choice,data}` outcome, covering both `complete` and `record-result`. No adoption action is required.

changes.summary: expose delegation history separately from Colony
changes.body:
Use `bee changelog` to read Bee's bundled release records without submitting
work or accessing a tracker. Bee and Colony retain separate tool histories
even though they share a package.

changes.summary: Managed bees retain configured harness paths under native daemon supervision, including the location of existing Codex authentication.
